correctness.rationale: An exact two-state Kolmogorov calculation gives the stated rational susceptibility. Both channel derivatives have strictly decreasing quadratic numerators for \(z\ge0\), establishing global peak classifications including equality. Strict monotonicity of \(H(g)=A_g(Q)/B_g(P)\), derived from its logarithmic derivative, gives exact existence/uniqueness precisely when \(Q/P>\sqrt{(1+\sqrt2)/2}\). Endpoint limits and forbidden positive-g equality are explicit. The standalone checker passed 500 complete inverse reconstructions, 1,500 independent matrix-response comparisons and 1,500 peak-derivative tests; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: Coalescence rates are natural physically interpretable observables in motional-narrowing spectroscopy. Their combination yields a global parameter identification and a sharp model-falsification inequality unavailable from either channel alone. The universal strict ratio and constructive inverse are nonlinear structural results; future use is for testing and calibrating telegraph frequency-noise models, with finite-sample stability unproved.
